{{short description|Topology in mathematics}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Stone–Čech remainder''' of a [[topological space]] ''X'', also called the '''corona''' or '''corona set''', is the [[complement (set theory)|complement]] {{nowrap|β''X'' \ ''X''}} of the space in its [[Stone–Čech compactification]] β''X''.

A topological space is said to be [[σ-compact space|σ-compact]] if it is the union of [[Countable set|countably]] many [[compact space|compact]] subspaces, and [[locally compact space|locally compact]] if every point has a [[neighbourhood (mathematics)|neighbourhood]] with compact [[closure (topology)|closure]]. The Stone–Čech remainder of a σ-compact and locally compact [[Hausdorff space]] is a [[sub-Stonean space]], i.e., any two [[open set|open]] σ-compact [[disjoint sets|disjoint]] subsets have disjoint compact closures.
